analysis.one_liner: Mazagon Dock Shipbuilders is a Mumbai-based defence PSU shipyard that builds and repairs warships and conventional submarines (including the Kalvari-class) almost entirely for the Indian Navy.
analysis.whats_happening: On 27 October 2026 Mazagon Dock reported Q2 FY27 revenue of ₹2,446 crore, down 16.5% YoY, with net profit falling 54% YoY to ₹344 crore as EBITDA margin collapsed to 8.1% from 23.8% a year earlier, hit by ₹445 crore of fresh provisions versus a provision reversal in the year-ago quarter. The board declared a ₹5/share interim dividend with record date 3 November 2026. The stock fell as much as 10-13% intraday to a fresh 52-week low around ₹1,687-1,705.
analysis.plain_terms: This is a Navy shipbuilder whose revenue depends on how fast it is executing a handful of very large, lumpy contracts. Right now the current order book (~₹16,443 crore) has thinned out faster than new mega-orders have been signed, so quarterly revenue has fallen for three straight quarters and a large one-off provision made this quarter's profit look especially weak. The market is betting heavily that a ~₹66,000-67,000 crore submarine order (Project-75I, with Germany's TKMS) gets signed soon to refill the pipeline - until it does, revenue recognition stays patchy. Don't read the 54% profit fall as a sign the underlying business is broken; it is an order-timing and provisioning story, not a demand problem.
analysis.quarters: Revenue/EBITDA margin/PAT by quarter: Sep'25 ₹2,929cr / 24% / ₹749cr; Dec'25 ₹3,601cr / 25% / ₹880cr; Mar'26 ₹3,850cr / 14% / ₹674cr; Jun'26 ₹2,943cr / 15% / ₹550cr; Sep'26 ₹2,446cr / 8% / ₹344cr. Revenue has now fallen in each of the last three quarters and the margin collapse in Sep'26 is largely a provisioning swing (₹445.5cr of fresh provisions versus a ₹25cr provision reversal a year ago) rather than a change in the underlying contract economics - treat the 8% margin quarter as not strictly comparable to the 23-25% margins of a year earlier. Management attributed the weakness to a depleting executable order book and delays in the P-75I submarine order converting to signed work.
analysis.performance_read: The stock is down 54.2% from its peak of ₹3,721 (29 May 2025) to the current ₹1,705, which also happens to be its 52-week low. This is an earnings-driven de-rating, not a corporate-action artifact - there was a 2:1 stock split in December 2024, but that is a straightforward share-count adjustment (not a demerger), so it does not understate returns the way a spin-off would. Over 1 year the stock (-37.4%) has fallen almost exactly in line with peer Cochin Shipyard (-37.1%), suggesting this is largely a sector-wide defence-order derating rather than company-specific mismanagement. Zoom out, though, and the 5-year return is still +1,305% versus Nifty's +29% - this is a stock unwinding part of an extraordinary prior re-rating, not a structural collapse.
analysis.valuation_read: At a trailing P/E of ~28x and P/B of ~6.6x against an ROE of ~29%, the stock is far cheaper than it was at its 2025 peak but not statistically cheap in absolute terms. It is cheap relative to its own recent history because the market has marked it down hard for the order-book gap and margin miss; whether it is actually cheap depends entirely on whether the P-75I submarine deal and other large pending contracts (LPDs, mine countermeasure vessels, 17B frigates, next-gen destroyers) get signed and executed at historical margins. If those orders slip further, the current multiple is being paid on a shrinking earnings base, not a growing one.
analysis.growth_read: Growth has stalled, not accelerated - revenue has declined sequentially for three quarters and operating margin has compressed sharply, so this is a margin-led deterioration rather than a volume story. The longer-run record (5-year profit CAGR of ~33.5%) was built on both volume and margin expansion, but that engine is currently paused pending new mega-contract signings; there is no current revenue growth to point to.
analysis.health_read: The company carries minimal debt and has historically run a cash-generative, advance-funded model typical of defence PSU shipyards, so balance-sheet leverage is not the risk here. The real risk is business/execution risk: whether provisions taken this quarter prove one-off, and whether cash conversion holds up as large contracts move through execution. Exact current net worth and cash-conversion figures could not be reliably cross-checked this round - not verified, check on Screener. A reported contingent liability figure of roughly ₹28,181 crore surfaced in one source and was not independently verified; flagging rather than stating as fact.
analysis.ownership_read: The Government of India holds 81.22% as promoter, with 0% of that stake pledged - about as low as governance/pledging risk gets for an Indian listed company. Institutional ownership is thin: FIIs hold just 0.26% and DIIs/mutual funds together under 7%, with public shareholders at 10.42%. No well-known marquee investor appears on the shareholding register based on the sources checked - worth saying plainly, since this is a stock retail investors have piled into without major institutional validation.
strengths: ROE of ~29% (3-year average ~32%) and ROCE of ~36% are well above typical industrial benchmarks
Zero promoter pledge on an 81.22% government promoter holding - minimal governance/ownership risk
Minimal debt on the balance sheet, typical of an advance-funded defence shipbuilder
Consistent dividend payer - ₹18.12/share TTM (~1.06% yield), plus the fresh ₹5/share interim declared with Q2 FY27 results
watchpoints: EBITDA margin fell from 23.8% (Q2 FY26) to 8.1% (Q2 FY27) on a ₹445.5cr swing in provisions - watch whether this reverses or recurs
Revenue has declined for three consecutive quarters (₹3,850cr → ₹2,943cr → ₹2,446cr) as the current order book (~₹16,443cr) thins faster than new orders are signed
Stock is down 54.2% from its May 2025 peak and sits at a fresh 52-week low; 3-month return of -28.27% is sharply worse than Nifty's -5.46%
A reported ~₹28,181cr contingent liability figure could not be independently verified - check the latest annual report notes on Screener before relying on it
analysis.one_thing: Whether the ~₹66,000-67,000 crore Project-75I submarine contract with TKMS gets formally signed and starts converting into revenue - that single event determines whether the current order-book gap and margin collapse are temporary (pending a mega-order) or the start of a structural slowdown.
analysis.data_notes: Q2 FY27 revenue, PAT, and EBITDA margin figures were cross-checked across multiple independent news sources (Upstox, Business Today, Business Upturn, Tradebrains) and are consistent. Shareholding and zero-pledge figures were cross-checked across Trendlyne and Choice India and agree. Could not independently verify the exact standalone net-worth/book-equity figure (one source's figure looked inconsistent with the quoted book value per share) or the ₹28,181cr contingent liability figure - both flagged as not verified rather than stated as fact.
